attribution.note: Zitron's own analysis in his newsletter, in his own voice.

semantics.note: Keeps the Scenario 1 condition (AI given free to lure customers) and the 'at best... every single time' wording. This is an analytic claim about the economics of bundling, so causal fits.

contract.note: Reading 'lose money' as incremental cost per interaction, before any offsetting sales, fits the next sentence and is an ordinary plain reading. The result depends on that reading and on how bundled revenue is treated, which the speaker never specified.

evidence.note: Atlassian's own notice confirms AI was included at no extra cost from May 2024. That establishes the scenario exists, not what each interaction cost or earned.
Box management says AI use was priced into Enterprise Plus and predicts no gross-margin dilution. This is a company statement and a forecast, not realized cost per interaction.

reviews.rationale: The packet confirms AI was bundled at no extra charge, and Box says the cost was priced into the plan. No evidence gives actual vendor cost per interaction or allocates subscription revenue. So neither the positive-incremental-cost reading nor the customer-loss reading can be settled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'What I believe will be a failed... attempt' states an unhedged expectation, so it is scored as a forecast. The rebrand description is an opinionated characterization folded into the proposition. No horizon was given.

contract.note: With no deadline, resolving only on terminal failure or a sustained, agent-attributed turnaround is a fair, ordinary reading. It does not invent a deadline.

evidence.note: Salesforce's own Q2 FY27 release (pre-cutoff) shows the agent business is ongoing, revenue growth of 11% that includes Informatica, and a redefined ARR. Reacceleration is only guided, not shown, so neither condition is met.
Secondary report of a partner survey showing subdued adoption. It does not measure Salesforce's revenue trajectory or show terminal failure.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and the early-resolution rule is not met. Agentforce has not been abandoned, and no sustained, agent-attributed reversal of revenue growth is shown. The CFO only forecasts a second-half reacceleration. Absence of success so far is not failure.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'multitudes higher' cost premise and the burden on any new revenue. 'Many times more' is a fair rendering.

contract.note: Reading 'multitudes' as several times, without a fixed multiplier, and requiring a matched-workload comparison are ordinary readings. Fixing the cost premise at the publication date is reasonable.

evidence.note: A Bain Capital Ventures estimate puts AI compute at about 1-3x hosting costs and says costs are falling. It has no matched sample, and the multiple is not clearly 'several times'.
Anthropic's prompt caching cuts some API costs. That challenges the idea of rising unit costs, but it does not measure SaaS service costs against conventional cloud.

reviews.rationale: The packet has one investor's estimate of AI compute at 1-3x hosting costs and evidence of falling unit prices. It has no matched-workload comparison and no financial link to SaaS revenue economics. Neither the cost multiple nor the causal burden is established or disproved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Keeps 'almost always' and limits the free-alternative point to the tasks he listed. 'Half-hearted' is opinion and is correctly left unscored.

contract.note: Reading 'almost always' as nearly universal and requiring a representative inventory is an ordinary reading. It also fairly flags that 'presentations' could mean slide text or a finished file.

evidence.note: Workday's own announcement shows generic content generation. It is a single example, not evidence of prevalence.
Box's own release shows drafting from GA in March 2024. Another example, but it does not measure the wider product population.
OpenAI's own announcement shows free ChatGPT with writing help, subject to usage limits. It partly covers the free-alternative point, but not finished presentations.

reviews.rationale: The examples match the kind of feature Zitron described, and free ChatGPT offered writing help. But no representative inventory shows near-universal prevalence among SaaS AI add-ons at publication. Free equivalence for presentations is also not shown.
